text: Hassan Emilio Kabande Laija, born on 15 June 1999 in Zapopan, Jalisco, Mexico, is known professionally as Peso Pluma and is a Mexican singer and rapper recognized for his work in regional Mexican music, particularly corridos tumbados. He began playing guitar at age 15 by watching YouTube videos and started writing songs in a diary, initially facing ridicule from peers, which later became a form of therapy as he realized some of his emotions could be expressed through rhymes. Kabande is the son of Hassan Kabande and Rubí Laija; his father was born in Chiapas and is of Lebanese descent, with ancestors emigrating from Bethlehem in the early 1900s, and his mother’s relatives were residents of Badiraguato, Sinaloa. He grew up in Guadalajara and began collaborating with his cousin, Roberto "Tito" Laija Garcia, also known as Tito Double P, on live albums Disco en Vivo (2020) and Disco en Vivo, Vol. 2 (2020), released by the independent label El Cartel de los Ángeles. His debut studio album, Ah y Qué? (2020), featured twelve songs and collaborations with El Choforo, Lalo Reyes, and Jorge Morales El Jilguero, followed by the single "Relajado Voy" released on 7 October. He released "Mil Historias" with Hector Rubio on 13 November and "El Petter" with Decreto Real on 4 December before launching his second studio album, Efectos Secundarios (2021), preceded by "Con Dinero Baila el Perro" and "Lo Que Me Das." The single "Por Las Noches," a slowed-down sierreño track about an unintended breakup, was released on 11 June. "Todo Es Playa," a song about smoking marijuana, was his last release with El Cartel de los Ángeles before switching to Prajin Records under George Prajin, with the socio-political track "Spiral" released on 25 November. On 4 February 2022, he released "El Belicón" with Raúl Vega, a corrido anthem on local narcoculture, which went viral after its music video, directed by Barush, gained 10 million YouTube views in one month and received significant playlisting on Spotify. The song debuted at number 50 on Billboard Hot Latin Songs, peaking at number 46, becoming his first chart entry. In April 2022, he released the EP Sembrando (2022), which included "Signal" and five new songs, celebrating fans and the 420 holiday, and was credited with solidifying the rise of corridos tumbados. He collaborated with Tornillos and Polo Gonzales on "Sentosa" for Garena Free Fire. On 3 June, he released "30 Tiros," an acoustic corrido about his success story, with a music video directed by Barush. In August 2022, he released "Siempre Pendientes" with Luis R. Conriquez, which sparked controversy for glorifying drug lord Joaquín "El Chapo" Guzmán, including lyrics such as "JGL, traigo en las cachas orgullosamente" and "Cuido la plaza del señor Guzmán," and a music video directed by Cesar Acosta that received 2 million views in 24 hours before being removed due to public outrage. At the 8 Music Fest in Culiacán on 1 October, Kabande performed the song live as a replacement for Junior H, with an image of El Chapo projected during the performance, drawing backlash from audiences, organizers, the city council, and netizens, with El Colectivo de Mujeres Activas Sinaloenses, A.C. (CMAS AC) denouncing the act and calling for sanctions under Article 254 of the Penal Code for the State of Sinaloa, potentially resulting in up to two years in prison. The city council defended the performance, stating it supported artistic freedom despite disapproving of the image projection. Kabande denied any connections to the cartel, stating he is an artist who only sings what he writes. In a 2023 interview with Pepe Garza, he said the controversy was "nothing that cannot be fixed" and continued with his career. "Siempre Pendientes" peaked at number 27 in Hot Latin Songs, 155 on Global Excl. U.S., and number 174 on Global 200, becoming his first global hit on Billboard, and debuted at number 9 on Mexico Songs, charting for 20 weeks. He announced "El Gavilán" as his next single on 21 October, released with Tony Aguirre and as his second collaboration with Conriquez, which reached number 41 in Hot Latin Songs by year-end. On 18 November, he released "Ando Enfocado" with Jaziel Aviles and Codiciado. On 24 November, he co-released "AMG" with Natanael Cano and Gabito Ballesteros, a song named after the Mercedes-AMG G 63, which debuted at number 25 on Mexico Songs and later reached number 10, becoming his first top-ten hit. The song, which featured a music video of the trio partying in Mexican nightlife with brass player footage, also debuted at number 92 on the Billboard Hot 100 with 5.8 million US streams, marking his first entry on the chart. "AMG" ascended to number 10 on Hot Latin Songs and reached number one on Mexico Songs on 25 February. On 9 December, he released "Delivery" with Alemán, introducing an experimental shift with hip-hop beats. On 30 December, Fuerza Regida released their album Pa Que Hablen (2022), which included the track "Igualito a Mi Apá" with Kabande. "PRC," released on 20 January, was written about the daily life of a gangster and became his second Hot 100 hit on 18 February, with a music video starring Cano and Kabande as dealers gaining 10 million views in its first week. The song's opening line, "Me levanto, un baño y luego me pongo a forjar," went viral on TikTok, sparking a dance craze and controversy due to children re-enacting it. On 10 February, Kabande and Junior H released "El Azul," a war corrido about working for El Chapo using his 701 moniker, which was censored by Spotify in late April for referencing fentanyl. The song debuted at number 15 on Mexico Songs. On 27 February, Argentine rapper Nicki Nicole remixed "Por Las Noches," adding a female perspective and a new verse, which fueled a resurgence of the original version on the Hot 100 on 25 March. On 9 March, he released "El Hechizo" with Colombian producer Ovy on the Drums, receiving rave reviews and a music video directed by Cristian Aguilar. His concert in León, Guanajuato, was postponed from 11 March to 30 March due to logistical and permit issues, creating buzz over possible government control due to his activism on narcoculture and his appeal among adolescents in a poor region. On 16 March, "Ella Baila Sola," a sierreño track written by Eslabón Armado's lead vocalist Pedro Tovar about friends spotting a beautiful girl on the dance floor, was officially released after a TikTok premiere. On 17 March, Kabande released a remix of Yng Lvcas' "La Bebé," aiming for a sonic shift, which was released with a music video on 23 March. "Ella Baila Sola" debuted at number 1 on both Latin Streaming Songs and Mexico Songs for the week ending 1 April, becoming both artists' first number-one single on Mexico Songs, and also debuted at number 2 on Hot Latin Songs, number 10 on Streaming Songs, and number 26 on the Hot 100, with 16 million official US streams in its first week. The "La Bebé" remix charted at number 77 on the Hot 100 with 6.8 million streams. With "AMG," "PRC," and "Por Las Noches" charting alongside "Ella Baila Sola" and "La Bebé," Kabande achieved the most Hot 100 Spanish-language entries for any Mexican artist. In celebration of his success, he announced the Doble P Tour across 17 U.S. cities. On 30 March, Becky G recruited Kabande for the single "Chanel," the first single from her regional Mexican album Esquinas, co-written with Tito and Grammy-winning producer Edgar Barrera, narrating a failed relationship. Kabande received updated Latin certifications from the Recording Industry Association of America, with "El Belicón" certified 8× Platinum for 480,000 units sold.

"Remix" charted at number 77 on the Hot 100 with 6.8 million streams in the United States. With "AMG", "PRC", and "Por Las Noches" charting alongside the releases of "Ella Baila Sola" and "La Bebé", Kabande achieved the most Hot 100 Spanish-language entries for any Mexican artist. In celebration of his success, he announced the Doble P Tour across 17 U.S. cities. Becky G recruited Kabande for the single "Chanel", released on 30 March as the first single from her regional Mexican album Esquinas; the track, co-written by the duo with Tito and Grammy-winning producer Edgar Barrera, tells the story of a failed relationship. The music video for "Chanel", directed by Ricky Alvarez and featuring performers in minimalistic outdoor settings, was released on 6 April. Becky G brought Kabande onstage during her Coachella 2023 set on 14 April for surprise performances of "Chanel" and "PRC". "Ella Baila Sola" reached number one on the daily Spotify Top 50 - Global chart on 15 April, dethroning "Flowers" by Miley Cyrus. During this period, the song topped the top 6 of the Mexico Songs chart and placed five songs in the top ten of the Hot Latin Songs chart, with "Ella Baila Sola" leading both. On 17 April, Billboard announced that "Ella Baila Sola" became the first regional Mexican top-ten song in the 64-year history of the Hot 100 after rising from 17 to 10. "El Azul" entered the Hot 100 at number 87, extending Kabande's record to six simultaneous entries. On 20 April, Kabande launched Double P Records in partnership with Prajin, signing artists Tito, Vega, and Jasiel Nuñez; he emphasized the label's goals of "making union, being grateful, and being humble" as CEO and head of A&R. His first single under the label, "Rosa Pastel" featuring Nuñez, was released to mark the label's foundation. At the 2023 Latin American Music Awards in Las Vegas, Nevada, Kabande joined Becky G onstage to perform "Chanel", marking his first American televised performance. On the weekly Spotify Global chart dated 20 April, "Ella Baila Sola" became the first Mexican act to reach number one. On 24 April, Billboard reported that "Ella Baila Sola" climbed from 10 to 5 on the Hot 100, becoming the first regional Mexican top-five hit in the chart's history. "Chanel" and "Igualito a Mi Apá" debuted at number 88 and 90, respectively, increasing Kabande's concurrent Hot 100 entries to eight in one week. "Ella Baila Sola" also reached number one on the Global 200, the first time a Mexican song achieved this. To promote the song, Kabande performed at The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon on 29 April, becoming the first regional Mexican artist to perform on the show; the event drew polarized reactions, with praise from fans and Mexican audiences for representation and criticism from critics over the absence of Eslabon Armado and concerns about narcoculture romanticization. On 1 May, "Ella Baila Sola" peaked at number 4 on the Hot 100. "AMG" was certified 7× Platinum with 420,000 units, and "El Azul" received 2× Platinum status. On 5 May, Puerto Rican rapper Eladio Carrión collaborated with Kabande on "77", a track about a luxurious lifestyle and work, with the music video directed by Jose Ovi Jimenez and released on 9 May. On 13 May, Anuel AA teased a collaboration with Kabande on social media, posting a photo of the singer at the Inglewood stop of his Legends Never Die Tour. Kabande released the solo track "Bye" on 26 May with a music video directed by Edgar Nito. On 31 May, Argentine producer Bizarrap featured Kabande on "Bzrp Music Sessions, Vol. 55". On June 22, Kabande released his third studio album, Génesis, supported by singles "Rosa Pastel", "77", and "Bye"; eight days later, a deluxe version was released, adding "PRC" with Natanael Cano, "Las Morras" with Blessd, and "Tulum" with Grupo Frontera. In July 2023, Génesis peaked at number 3 on the Billboard 200, becoming the highest-charting and fastest-selling regional Mexican album in Billboard history. In September 2023, Kabande became the first música mexicana star to perform at the MTV Video Music Awards. Later that month, he canceled an October 14 show in Tijuana, Mexico after being threatened by banners signed with the initials of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel. In October, American singer Arcángel and Kabande released "La Chamba", the lead single from Arcángel's fifth studio album. In November, Kabande released "Peligro" in promotion of the 2023 video game Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III, and at the end of November, he released "Una Bala" with Milo J, part of Milo J's debut album 111. Days later, Brazilian singer Anitta collaborated with Kabande on "Bellakeo". Kabande later released "Rompe la Dompe" with Junior H and Óscar Maydon as the final single of 2023. Speculation from interviews and live performances in 2023 suggested a collaborative EP with Jasiel Nuñez in 2024 and a fourth studio album. In early 2024, Kabande released "Pixelados" with Luis R. Conriquez as his first song of the year. He was invited to the 2024 Viña del Mar International Song Festival, but the invitation faced criticism from Chilean public intellectual Alberto Mayol for exalting narcoculture; councilor René Lues wrote an open letter urging the city council to recall the invitation, and Chilean ministers of interior and justice, Carolina Tohá and Luis Cordero Vega, joined the criticism. The controversy was widely covered internationally. In late January 2024, Kabande released singles as a secondary artist on the Hot 100, including "Igual que un Ángel" with Kali Uchis and "La Intención" with Christian Nodal. At the 66th Annual Grammy Awards, Kabande won Best Música Mexicana Album (including Tejano) for Génesis (2023). In February 2024, after a video of Kabande with another woman in Las Vegas went viral, Nicki Nicole officially announced their breakup, with most of their social media posts deleted. After the breakup, Kabande released the bachata-infused song "A Tu Manera" with Junior H, followed a week later by the Latin rap single "No Son Klle" with Santa Fe Klan and Duki. Kabande announced his second headlining tour, Éxodo Tour, and revealed his fourth studio album Éxodo in an interview with Rolling Stone, becoming the first Mexican artist to appear on Rolling Stone's front cover. He collaborated with Tito Double P and Joel de la P on the sequel track "La People II", which debuted at number 69 on the Hot 100, marking the first chart appearances for both artists. He also released a reggaeton track with Chencho Corleone titled "Humo". A day before his Coachella 2024 performance, he announced a collaboration with Arcángel titled "Peso Completo", confirming it as part of Éxodo. He released a trailer featuring Irish MMA fighter Conor McGregor, revealing the album's release date and the single "La Durango". On 17 April 2024, he joined DJ Snake on the electronic dance track "Teka". It was speculated he would collaborate with Junior H and Eslabon Armado after sharing an animated clip on Instagram; "La Durango" by all three artists was released on 9 May 2024 and performed with Pedro Tovar of Eslabon Armado on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon. He collaborated with Gabito Ballesteros on "Sin Yolanda", released alongside the latter's debut album The GB on 24 May 2024. On the same day, he released "Gimme a Second" with American rapper Rich the Kid. On the same day, Kabande revealed the cover art and tracklist for Éxodo, which includes collaborations with Chino Pacas, Iván Cornejo, Cardi B, Quavo, among others. Éxodo debuted at number five on the US Billboard 200 with 64,000 album-equivalent units, consisting of 87.51 million official streams across all 24 tracks, and topped the US Top Latin Albums and Regional Mexican Albums charts, earning his second number-one album on both. "Vino Tinto", a collaborative song with Natanael Cano and Ballesteros from Éxodo, was released as the eighth single on 26 June 2024 and peaked at number four in Mexico. "Tommy & Pamela", a collaboration with Kenia Os and its music video, was released as the ninth single on 18 July 2024. On 8 August 2024, Kabande released "Los Cuadros" with cousin Tito Double P, along with its music video. On the same day, he featured on "Drunk" with American rapper Kodak Black, part of the digital deluxe version of ¥$'s Vultures 2 (2024). On 22 August, he appeared on "Dos Días" by Tito Double P from the latter's debut album Incómodo (2024) and on "Se Te Nota" by Myke Towers from the latter's album La Pantera Negra (2024). "La Patrulla" with Netón Vega and its music video was released as the tenth single on 5 September 2024. Following Hurricane Milton, Kabande canceled his final two Éxodo Tour dates—16 October at Amalie Arena in Tampa, Florida, and 17 October at Kaseya Center in Miami—with the tour concluding on 13 October in Greensboro. Éxodo received a nomination for Best Música Mexicana Album (including Tejano) at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards in February 2025, making it Kabande's second Grammy nomination. On 7 November, he appeared on Jasiel Nuñez's second studio album La Odisea (2024), contributing to "California Sunset", "Amiri" with Tito Double P, and "En Mi Mundo". He also participated in Netón Vega's album Mi Vida Mi Muerte with a duet titled "Morena". He appeared on the Billboard Global 200 with "Dopamina", which peaked at number 20 in its second week of release. Kabande recalled that he always listened to reggaeton, hip-hop, and rap, but realized his voice was made for singing corridos because he heard them played around family, noting that his voice shined differently in that genre. He cites Ariel Camacho and Valentín Elizalde as his primary musical influences, interpreting their songs as a young man. He is an avid hip-hop listener, citing Canadian rapper Drake as his favorite artist, reflecting his experience growing up across borders, and also references the Weeknd, 21 Savage, Post Malone, Suicideboys, and Shoreline Mafia as influences. After becoming the top streamed artist in Mexico, media outlets have compared his success to Puerto Rican artist Bad Bunny. Despite this, Kabande has repeatedly acknowledged Bunny as a musical inspiration, having privately conversed with him during Coachella 2023, stating there are only good things to say about him and expressing admiration and respect. Bunny publicly debunked rumors of conflict by posting a video with Kendall Jenner singing along to "AMG" on his Instagram Stories. In 2025, Kabande became the first Mexican ambassador of the Council of Fashion Designers of America (CFDA) for New York Fashion Week, making his official debut at the CFDA cocktail event at Rockefeller Center in a design by Willy Chavarría styled by Anastasia Walker. According to a report by El Gordo y la Flaca on 12 May 2023, Kabande purchased a 174 m² apartment in the Andares district of Puerta de Hierro, Zapopan, for approximately MXN$14,400,000 (US$800,000), which serves as his official residence. He has expressed interest in soccer; in his youth, he played for the junior teams of C.D. Guadalajara, though he is a supporter of their city rivals, Atlas F.C. Kabande made his official debut at the Council of Fashion Designers of America (CFDA) cocktail event at Rockefeller Center, wearing a design by Willy Chavarría styled by Anastasia Walker. On 12 May 2023, El Gordo y la Flaca reported that Kabande purchased a 174 m² apartment in the Andares district of Puerta de Hierro, Zapopan, for approximately MXN$14,400,000 (US$800,000), which functions as his official residence. He has shown an interest in soccer; during his youth, he played for the junior teams of C.D. Guadalajara, though he is a supporter of their city rivals, Atlas F.C. In July 2023, rumors emerged that Kabande was dating Argentine singer Nicki Nicole, who initially denied the claims, stating they were only friends, but later confirmed their relationship in November 2023. In February 2024, after a video surfaced showing Kabande with another woman in Las Vegas, Nicole announced the end of their relationship. In August 2024, Kabande confirmed he was in a relationship with American influencer Hanna Howell, who had previously hinted at the romance on social media. In September 2024, Howell announced their breakup, stating that Kabande had returned all of her belongings except for her pet dog. In January 2025, speculation arose that Kabande was romantically involved with Mexican singer Kenia OS. The couple publicly confirmed their relationship in April 2025 during the Coachella festival.
